name: Project board
description: The GitHub Project that tracks this repository's work (project.json names it), as a board grouped by Status, with tools for agents to list items, see what needs a decision, set Status, Priority or Area, and add issues and pull requests. Its screen reads an issue or pull request in place and saves the owner's answer to an item that needs a decision on this computer only, never on GitHub; agents list those (list_owner_answers), record each in English with comment and mark it recorded (mark_answer_recorded). It also carries the repository's CI and merge procedure: ci_status (required checks, the first failing test line, known intermittent failures). queue_merge, for maintainers only, squash-merges PRs or a stack on its own once every required check is reported and passed (never auto-merge), telling the queuing session when one needs it. And the contribution procedure: open_pr (the repository's pull request template filled, refusing an empty Not exercised), file_issue and comment (English only; refusing words from a private list kept in the app's data folder, editable on its screen and with edit_private_words), commit_check (docs/commit-conventions.md, refusing attribution lines), and rebase_stack (a stacked pull request moved onto its base after the one under it was squash-merged, confirming the change is the one tested). And the release (docs/releasing.md): release_status (where it stands, the notes draft, the next step; the screen's Release dialog) and release (maintainer only: rehearse, tag, approve; each step refuses unless its checks pass, and does nothing without confirm). Reads and writes go through the person's own GitHub CLI (`gh`): the app stores no token and asks Centralu for nothing. It needs `gh` installed and logged in, with the `project` scope for the board (`gh auth refresh -s project`); when it is not, or GitHub cannot be reached, the board and the tools say so.

uses.background: drives the merge queue while it has pull requests to land
